- RECIPE FIX — `cnp-and-dline-calibration` step 3 D-offset: the minimum of R_CNP along the ridge vs raw D is a usable "physically locates D = 0" feature (run 5: vertex at raw D = +0.013 V/nm, symmetric R on both sides); worth naming as the default feature to look for.
- TOOLING — `hera-watch` ETA on a mixed-step field sweep (50 mT then 10 mT) extrapolates the current per-row rate (24 s/pt on the coarse leg → "6 h"); a per-setpoint-spacing model (ramp time ∝ ΔB + fixed overhead) would price it right.

1	# Rig card — VTI
2	
3	*Rig-level machine facts for the Sharpe Lab VTI (variable-temperature
4	insert) cryostat. Canonical copy: `hera/rig-cards/VTI.md` in the
5	`measurement-env` repo; deployed as `rig_card.md` next to
6	`device_card.md` in the measurement directory. Errors or gaps found
7	in-session go to `session_notes.md`, not this file — agents are
8	read-only on the repo.*
9	
10	## Identity
11	- **Rig**: VTI — wet variable-temperature insert (closed-loop He
12	  recirculation), out-of-plane magnet
13	- **Rig owner**: Bingcheng (VTI czar) — adjudicates envelope and
14	  operating-edge questions
15	- **Control PC**: `dgg-vti` (Windows 11); measurement dirs under
16	  `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`
17	- **Base temperature**: ≈ 1.2–1.3 K; electron temperature ≈ 8 K
18	- **Status**: in service
19	
20	## Magnet
21	
22	- **Supply / driver**: CAEN ELS FAST-PS 1K5, `drivers.FastBi1K5`
23	  (raw TCP `192.168.0.10:10001`). Out-of-plane field, Tesla, via the
24	  `field` qcodes Parameter.
25	- **Coil constant**: `T_per_A = 1/7.3` ≈ 0.137 T/A.
26	- **Ramp rate**: fixed 1 A/min ≈ **0.137 T/min**, hard-coded in the
27	  driver and sent with every setpoint. An 8 T traverse is a ~58 min
28	  floor.
29	- **Set semantics**: `magnet.field(target)` **blocks** until the field
30	  is reached (polls the ramping flag, then a `settle_s` dwell — default
31	  3 s, tunable). A cell that ramps is busy the whole ramp.
32	- **Interrupt ≠ stop**: interrupting the notebook cell does **not**
33	  stop the supply — it keeps ramping to the last setpoint. There is no
34	  abort/pause/ramp-to-zero method; recovery is calling `field()` again
35	  with a new target. Aborting a ramp is the operator acting on the
36	  instrument, never a kernel interrupt.
37	- **Magnet limit**: **14.0 T** (Zack ruling 2026-06-12), enforced by
38	  the driver (`max_field_T = 14.0`; ramping above it raises). The
39	  session cap (device card / SAFETIES, machine-enforced via
40	  `magnet.field.vals`) is what measurements obey.
41	- **High field + elevated T interact through the probe's coupling to
42	  the bath**; not expected to bite below ~100 K (heuristic — Aaron,
43	  2026-08-02, bath-vs-probe-T response unmeasured).
44	- **Read-truth**: `field()`'s get returns the **measured** output
45	  current × `T_per_A` (`GET:I:?`, 2-stage moving-average readback,
46	  ~41 ms lag ≈ 0.1 mT at our slew). The set-point is not readable as
47	  field; never infer field from the last set call.
48	- **Persistent switch / output**: heater `heater_on()` / `heater_off()`
49	  (each blocks 10 s, **no field-matching check** — operator-only);
50	  state reads `magnet.persistent_switch_on()`, `magnet.output_enabled()`.
51	- **Never re-traverse**: the fixed slow ramp makes field the expensive
52	  axis. Plan sweeps to start where the magnet sits and end where the
53	  next measurement needs it; alternate fan directions across
54	  iterations rather than returning to a preferred start field.
55	
56	## Thermometry & heaters
57	
58	- **Controller**: Lakeshore 335 (`drivers.Lakeshore_335`).
59	  Input A = sample-mount Cernox (`sample_temperature`, `KRDG? A`);
60	  input B = vaporizer Cernox (`vaporizer_temperature`, `KRDG? B`).
61	- **Readout is file-based, never GPIB**: the lakeshore worker (VTI
62	  Monitor launcher) owns LS335 polling and writes InfluxDB (`vti`) plus
63	  `C:\Users\DGG\temperature_logs\VTI_{sample,vaporizer}.txt`. Logfile
64	  cadence **5 s** (InfluxDB 30 s; worker `READ_INTERVAL`, 2026-07-16).
65	  Freshness guards must allow **≥ 2–3 write periods** — a threshold
66	  equal to the cadence false-fires at end-of-period (burned: ladder v2,
67	  2026-07-15). The kernel
68	  reads `T_sample` / `T_vaporizer` via
69	  `temperature_from_logfiles(VTI.temp_logfile_candidates[...])`,
70	  `fp()`-able as recorded channels; the `heater` instance is control-only
71	  (setpoints / ranges / power). A frozen logfile (dead worker) reads a
72	  plausible value that `assert T < base` cannot catch — at bring-up
73	  confirm the logfile mtime is advancing.
74	- **Sensors**: 2× CX-1030-CU-HT-0.3M (serials X225149, X225150),
75	  NIST-traceable ITS-90, 0.3–420 K. Calibration packages in-repo at
76	  `hera/vti/cernox-cal/` (INDEX.md has the error budget). Curve
77	  assignments (read from NVRAM 2026-06-12): **input A = curve 23,
78	  serial X225149**; input B = curve 21, whose header *also* reads
79	  X225149 — likely X225150's data loaded under an unedited name, or a
80	  duplicate load of A's curve. Impact is bounded by the inter-sensor
81	  cal delta and B is control-only, but the anomaly is unresolved
82	  (Bingcheng).
83	- **Accuracy**: ±6–9 mK at 10–20 K, zero-field. Field-induced error:
84	  order tens of mK at 10 K / 6 T (CX-1030 magnetoresistance runs a
85	  few× the published CX-1050 table), negligible above ~30 K. B is
86	  logged per point, so the field term is a clean post-hoc correction.
87	- **Control topology**: both LS335 loops are closed-loop (loop 1
88	  sample-mount heater ↔ input A; loop 2 vaporizer ↔ input B). The
89	  sanctioned elevated-T method is **`heater.set_both(T, ratio=0.95)`**,
90	  authorized **≤ 100 K** (Aaron, 2026-07-18, via Zack). The **needle
91	  valve remains operator-only, hands at the rig**.
92	- **Sample-loop PID is untuned** (confirmed live 2026-07-15): upward
93	  setpoint steps overshoot **~+1.4 K**, and recovery is bath-limited —
94	  the sample cools only toward the vaporizer floor at `ratio·T`, so
95	  the overshoot penalty scales with (1 − ratio). At ratio 0.99:
96	  ~0.015 K/min recovery; tolerance-settling never passed below ~20 K.
97	  Accept elevated-T points on *stability*, not proximity (hover
98	  acceptance — temperature-dependence VTI variant). Tuning backlogged
99	  (eng-backlog, Bingcheng).
100	- **Offsets**: the mount→device thermal gradient is **uncharacterized**
101	  (heater-power dependent). Treat absolute-T claims accordingly; LK
102	  fits inherit T errors linearly. Ask the operator.
103	
104	
105	## Silent preconditions
106	
107	Per the prompt's "preflight the silent preconditions" working-style
108	bullet — state sweeps depend on but never set, with the cheap read for
109	each. (LS335 control instance is named `heater`; temperature is read from
110	the worker logfiles via `T_sample` / `T_vaporizer`.)
111	
112	| Hazard | One-line read | Expected at rest | Why silent |
113	|---|---|---|---|
114	| Sample temperature | `T_sample()` | ≈ 1.2–1.3 K at base | every sweep assumes T; almost none set it |
115	| Magnet field | `magnet.field()` (measured readback) | wherever the last ramp ended — read, never assume 0 | gate sweeps inherit B from prior cells |
116	| Vaporizer state | `T_vaporizer()` | tracks base unless a ladder is in progress | needle-valve setting is manual and persists across cells |
117	| PS heater / output | `magnet.persistent_switch_on()`, `magnet.output_enabled()` | heater on, output enabled (`field()` raises otherwise) | touched only at bring-up |
118	
119	## Sweep stack & data layout
120	
121	The `sweep` package (measureme submodule) is the single source of truth for the
122	station/sweep call surface, the on-disk run format, and the metadata schema:
123	`docs/api/measureme.md`. Stations are built with `sweep.AsyncStation`. Rig
124	specifics:
125	
126	- **Measurement dir**: each sweep writes `<measurement_dir>/data/<file_id>/`,
127	  the measurement dir being `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`.
128	- **`plot.png` is the live monitor, not the measurement** — for rastered /
129	  co-swept maps it does not show the physical map; re-form from the TSV before
130	  any visual read.
131	- **Mixed metadata on disk**: this rig's corpus spans both schema versions
132	  (older singular keys; current plural + `version`/`instruments`). Load through
133	  `hera.analysis` / `sweep.sweep_load`, never hand-rolled.
134	
135	## Timing rules of thumb
136	
137	Defaults for wall-clock arithmetic — calibrate against runs in the
138	current measurement dir before pricing anything long, and cite the
139	calibrating run.
140	
141	- **Per-point ≈ dwell + readback.** Instrument reads serialize:
142	  ~25–30 ms per read, SR830 X+P batching into one SNAP?. Standard fp
143	  set ≈ **0.2–0.25 s/pt** at NPLC=1 (20260714.2 run 4; 2026-06-14
144	  fan); ~1.1 s/pt with the 2400s at NPLC=10 (pA-floor gate-current
145	  reads, typical until early leakage checks are done — 20260714.2
146	  runs 0–3). Include NPLC when recording a timing calibration.
147	- **Gatemap row turnaround ≈ flyback**: the fast axis steps home at
148	  `volt.step`, ~6 ms/write — span/`volt.step` × 6 ms + slow_delay
149	  (run 4: 6 V at 5 mV + slow_delay=3 → 12 s/row); scales with the
150	  fast span. Fan wall-clock ÷ points (~2.1 s/pt, run 7) folds ramps +
151	  turnaround in — not a per-point rate.
152	- **Fan arithmetic**: wall-clock ≈ B_span / 0.137 T/min (ramp floor)
153	  + N_rows × (N_fast × per-point + row turnaround).
154	- **Row turnaround**: ~60 s/row at fine B steps (run 5, 2026-06-10:
155	  121 rows × 271 pts, predicted 12.3 h vs actual 13.6 h). At coarse
156	  steps rows are ramp-limited instead (run 3: 278 s/row at 0.25 T
157	  steps ≈ 110 s ramp + turnaround).
158	- **Measured ramps are slower than bare ramps**: a field traverse
159	  recorded as a sweep moves at ~0.092 T/min effective (per-point
160	  overhead on top of the 0.137 bare rate) — ~40% more wall-clock than
161	  an unrecorded ramp. Usually still worth it; price honestly.
162	- **Closed-loop T settles run 2–5 min** on this rig (2026-06-10/12
163	  ladder, ~54 min/pt dominated by sweeps) — not the 10–20 min of
164	  toploader lore. Don't inherit settle budgets across rigs. Up-leg
165	  catches 2.5–4 min (2026-07-15 ladder); descents are
166	  passive-cooling-limited (τ ≈ 27 min measured 34→25 K at ratio 0.99)
167	  — see the temperature-dependence VTI variant's descend-catch pattern.
168	
169	## Standard equipment
170	
171	Racked inventory with defaults; anything marked **(per-device)** is a
172	hole the device card fills, and the device card wins any conflict.
173	
174	- **Lock-ins**: SR830 family, 4 in recent service (`sr0…sr3`). Channel
175	  roles, gains, sensitivities, contact pairs: (per-device).
176	  **Settling**: `time_constant` + `filter_slope` are operator-set on the
177	  front panel and **not set by the kit** — read them (`srN.time_constant()`,
178	  `srN.filter_slope()`) at bring-up and record them, so the swept-point dwell
179	  (`≳ k·τ`; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct) can be priced against a
180	  known τ and bent knowingly, not guessed (STYLE rule 12 settling floor). The
181	  run-metadata `instruments` snapshot currently stores these as `None` —
182	  until that's fixed, the bring-up record is the only place τ lives on disk.
183	- **Current preamp**: Ithaco transimpedance preamp on the drain
184	  channel; gain setting (per-device), recorded per run in
185	  `measurement_config`.
186	- **DC sources**: SRS DC205 (serial, 115200 baud, **ASRL7**,
187	  s/n 20500514) — use `drivers.SRS_DC205` (rate-based ramp,
188	  deterministic dV/dt); the
189	  `sharpelab_nb` driver of the same name has different ramp semantics
190	  and they are **not interchangeable**. 2× Keithley 2400 for gates.
191	  The Keithley `volt.step`, the DC205 `ramp_rate`, and `inter_delay` are
192	  operator-owned — the agent never changes them.
193	- **Contact mux**: QDevil QSwitch (expected IDN: serial 37, firmware
194	  2.0) via `drivers.QSwitch` + `drivers.contact_mux.ContactMux`.
195	  **Max signal voltage 60 V DC** (30 Vrms / 42 Vpp AC) — QDevil's rated
196	  limit (`docs/manuals/qswitch/`, §3.1 + specifications table); every
197	  signal line routed through the switch must stay within it.
198	  USB-CDC serial (Microchip VID_04D8), **ASRL4**.
199	  Switching grounds lines during transitions; `settle_s` default 10 s
200	  (read `mux.settle_s`).
201	  Per-cooldown bless status (validated address, any `settle_s` override)
202	  lives in the device card; `ContactMux` is live only when the device
203	  card says so. The `lines`/`breakouts` maps are wiring → (per-device).
204	- **Terranova 906A gauge**: serial, **ASRL8** — held by the
205	  influx-logger kernel.
206	- **He level**: AMI Model 1700 (`drivers.AMI_1700`),
207	  `192.168.0.100:7180` (s/n 1700-20-207).
208	- **Instrument LAN** (isolated 192.168.0/24): `.10` FastBi supply,
209	  `.100` AMI 1700, `.101` this PC, `.1` router.
210	
211	## Known quirks
212	
213	- Console is cp1252; `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` is set in `~/.bashrc`
214	  to address unicode issues.
215	
216	## What this card does not carry
217	
218	- **Device facts** — wiring/contact maps, gains, gate stacks,
219	  validators, calibrated settle times → device card.
220	- **Campaign state** — goals, recipes in play, reference runs → brief.
221	- **Session caps** — field/T/voltage limits chosen for a session →
222	  device card + SAFETIES cell.
223	- **Conclusions** — no prior-campaign operating points, no device
224	  leans, no "last time X worked". This card is agent-visible during
225	  blinded sessions, and operational defaults are also information.

  session cap (device card / SAFETIES, machine-enforced via
  `magnet.field.vals`) is what measurements obey.
- **High field + elevated T interact through the probe's coupling to
  the bath**; not expected to bite below ~100 K (heuristic — Aaron,
  2026-08-02, bath-vs-probe-T response unmeasured).
- **Read-truth**: `field()`'s get returns the **measured** output
  current × `T_per_A` (`GET:I:?`, 2-stage moving-average readback,
  ~41 ms lag ≈ 0.1 mT at our slew). The set-point is not readable as
  field; never infer field from the last set call.
- **Persistent switch / output**: heater `heater_on()` / `heater_off()`
  (each blocks 10 s, **no field-matching check** — operator-only);
  state reads `magnet.persistent_switch_on()`, `magnet.output_enabled()`.
- **Never re-traverse**: the fixed slow ramp makes field the expensive
  axis. Plan sweeps to start where the magnet sits and end where the
  next measurement needs it; alternate fan directions across
  iterations rather than returning to a preferred start field.

## Thermometry & heaters

- **Controller**: Lakeshore 335 (`drivers.Lakeshore_335`).
  Input A = sample-mount Cernox (`sample_temperature`, `KRDG? A`);
  input B = vaporizer Cernox (`vaporizer_temperature`, `KRDG? B`).
- **Readout is file-based, never GPIB**: the lakeshore worker (VTI
  Monitor launcher) owns LS335 polling and writes InfluxDB (`vti`) plus
  `C:\Users\DGG\temperature_logs\VTI_{sample,vaporizer}.txt`. Logfile
  cadence **5 s** (InfluxDB 30 s; worker `READ_INTERVAL`, 2026-07-16).
  Freshness guards must allow **≥ 2–3 write periods** — a threshold
  equal to the cadence false-fires at end-of-period (burned: ladder v2,
  2026-07-15). The kernel
  reads `T_sample` / `T_vaporizer` via
  `temperature_from_logfiles(VTI.temp_logfile_candidates[...])`,
  `fp()`-able as recorded channels; the `heater` instance is control-only
  (setpoints / ranges / power). A frozen logfile (dead worker) reads a
  plausible value that `assert T < base` cannot catch — at bring-up
  confirm the logfile mtime is advancing.
- **Sensors**: 2× CX-1030-CU-HT-0.3M (serials X225149, X225150),
  NIST-traceable ITS-90, 0.3–420 K. Calibration packages in-repo at
  `hera/vti/cernox-cal/` (INDEX.md has the error budget). Curve
  assignments (read from NVRAM 2026-06-12): **input A = curve 23,
  serial X225149**; input B = curve 21, whose header *also* reads
  X225149 — likely X225150's data loaded under an unedited name, or a
  duplicate load of A's curve. Impact is bounded by the inter-sensor
  cal delta and B is control-only, but the anomaly is unresolved
  (Bingcheng).
- **Accuracy**: ±6–9 mK at 10–20 K, zero-field. Field-induced error:
  order tens of mK at 10 K / 6 T (CX-1030 magnetoresistance runs a
  few× the published CX-1050 table), negligible above ~30 K. B is
  logged per point, so the field term is a clean post-hoc correction.
- **Control topology**: both LS335 loops are closed-loop (loop 1
  sample-mount heater ↔ input A; loop 2 vaporizer ↔ input B). The
  sanctioned elevated-T method is **`heater.set_both(T, ratio=0.95)`**,
  authorized **≤ 100 K** (Aaron, 2026-07-18, via Zack). The **needle
  valve remains operator-only, hands at the rig**.
- **Sample-loop PID is untuned** (confirmed live 2026-07-15): upward
  setpoint steps overshoot **~+1.4 K**, and recovery is bath-limited —
  the sample cools only toward the vaporizer floor at `ratio·T`, so
  the overshoot penalty scales with (1 − ratio). At ratio 0.99:
  ~0.015 K/min recovery; tolerance-settling never passed below ~20 K.
  Accept elevated-T points on *stability*, not proximity (hover
  acceptance — temperature-dependence VTI variant). Tuning backlogged
  (eng-backlog, Bingcheng).
- **Offsets**: the mount→device thermal gradient is **uncharacterized**
  (heater-power dependent). Treat absolute-T claims accordingly; LK
  fits inherit T errors linearly. Ask the operator.


## Silent preconditions

Per the prompt's "preflight the silent preconditions" working-style
bullet — state sweeps depend on but never set, with the cheap read for
each. (LS335 control instance is named `heater`; temperature is read from
the worker logfiles via `T_sample` / `T_vaporizer`.)

| Hazard | One-line read | Expected at rest | Why silent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sample temperature | `T_sample()` | ≈ 1.2–1.3 K at base | every sweep assumes T; almost none set it |
| Magnet field | `magnet.field()` (measured readback) | wherever the last ramp ended — read, never assume 0 | gate sweeps inherit B from prior cells |
| Vaporizer state | `T_vaporizer()` | tracks base unless a ladder is in progress | needle-valve setting is manual and persists across cells |
| PS heater / output | `magnet.persistent_switch_on()`, `magnet.output_enabled()` | heater on, output enabled (`field()` raises otherwise) | touched only at bring-up |

## Sweep stack & data layout

The `sweep` package (measureme submodule) is the single source of truth for the
station/sweep call surface, the on-disk run format, and the metadata schema:
`docs/api/measureme.md`. Stations are built with `sweep.AsyncStation`. Rig
specifics:

- **Measurement dir**: each sweep writes `<measurement_dir>/data/<file_id>/`,
  the measurement dir being `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`.
- **`plot.png` is the live monitor, not the measurement** — for rastered /
  co-swept maps it does not show the physical map; re-form from the TSV before
  any visual read.
- **Mixed metadata on disk**: this rig's corpus spans both schema versions
  (older singular keys; current plural + `version`/`instruments`). Load through
  `hera.analysis` / `sweep.sweep_load`, never hand-rolled.

## Timing rules of thumb

Defaults for wall-clock arithmetic — calibrate against runs in the
current measurement dir before pricing anything long, and cite the
calibrating run.

- **Per-point ≈ dwell + readback.** Instrument reads serialize:
  ~25–30 ms per read, SR830 X+P batching into one SNAP?. Standard fp
  set ≈ **0.2–0.25 s/pt** at NPLC=1 (20260714.2 run 4; 2026-06-14
  fan); ~1.1 s/pt with the 2400s at NPLC=10 (pA-floor gate-current
  reads, typical until early leakage checks are done — 20260714.2
  runs 0–3). Include NPLC when recording a timing calibration.
- **Gatemap row turnaround ≈ flyback**: the fast axis steps home at
  `volt.step`, ~6 ms/write — span/`volt.step` × 6 ms + slow_delay
  (run 4: 6 V at 5 mV + slow_delay=3 → 12 s/row); scales with the
  fast span. Fan wall-clock ÷ points (~2.1 s/pt, run 7) folds ramps +
  turnaround in — not a per-point rate.
- **Fan arithmetic**: wall-clock ≈ B_span / 0.137 T/min (ramp floor)
  + N_rows × (N_fast × per-point + row turnaround).
- **Row turnaround**: ~60 s/row at fine B steps (run 5, 2026-06-10:
  121 rows × 271 pts, predicted 12.3 h vs actual 13.6 h). At coarse
  steps rows are ramp-limited instead (run 3: 278 s/row at 0.25 T
  steps ≈ 110 s ramp + turnaround).
- **Measured ramps are slower than bare ramps**: a field traverse
  recorded as a sweep moves at ~0.092 T/min effective (per-point
  overhead on top of the 0.137 bare rate) — ~40% more wall-clock than
  an unrecorded ramp. Usually still worth it; price honestly.
- **Closed-loop T settles run 2–5 min** on this rig (2026-06-10/12
  ladder, ~54 min/pt dominated by sweeps) — not the 10–20 min of
  toploader lore. Don't inherit settle budgets across rigs. Up-leg
  catches 2.5–4 min (2026-07-15 ladder); descents are
  passive-cooling-limited (τ ≈ 27 min measured 34→25 K at ratio 0.99)
  — see the temperature-dependence VTI variant's descend-catch pattern.

## Standard equipment

Racked inventory with defaults; anything marked **(per-device)** is a
hole the device card fills, and the device card wins any conflict.

- **Lock-ins**: SR830 family, 4 in recent service (`sr0…sr3`). Channel
  roles, gains, sensitivities, contact pairs: (per-device).
  **Settling**: `time_constant` + `filter_slope` are operator-set on the
  front panel and **not set by the kit** — read them (`srN.time_constant()`,
  `srN.filter_slope()`) at bring-up and record them, so the swept-point dwell
  (`≳ k·τ`; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct) can be priced against a
  known τ and bent knowingly, not guessed (STYLE rule 12 settling floor). The
  run-metadata `instruments` snapshot currently stores these as `None` —
  until that's fixed, the bring-up record is the only place τ lives on disk.
- **Current preamp**: Ithaco transimpedance preamp on the drain
  channel; gain setting (per-device), recorded per run in
  `measurement_config`.
- **DC sources**: SRS DC205 (serial, 115200 baud, **ASRL7**,
  s/n 20500514) — use `drivers.SRS_DC205` (rate-based ramp,
  deterministic dV/dt); the
  `sharpelab_nb` driver of the same name has different ramp semantics
  and they are **not interchangeable**. 2× Keithley 2400 for gates.
  The Keithley `volt.step`, the DC205 `ramp_rate`, and `inter_delay` are
  operator-owned — the agent never changes them.
- **Contact mux**: QDevil QSwitch (expected IDN: serial 37, firmware
  2.0) via `drivers.QSwitch` + `drivers.contact_mux.ContactMux`.
  **Max signal voltage 60 V DC** (30 Vrms / 42 Vpp AC) — QDevil's rated
  limit (`docs/manuals/qswitch/`, §3.1 + specifications table); every
  signal line routed through the switch must stay within it.
  USB-CDC serial (Microchip VID_04D8), **ASRL4**.
  Switching grounds lines during transitions; `settle_s` default 10 s
  (read `mux.settle_s`).
  Per-cooldown bless status (validated address, any `settle_s` override)
  lives in the device card; `ContactMux` is live only when the device
  card says so. The `lines`/`breakouts` maps are wiring → (per-device).
- **Terranova 906A gauge**: serial, **ASRL8** — held by the
  influx-logger kernel.
- **He level**: AMI Model 1700 (`drivers.AMI_1700`),
  `192.168.0.100:7180` (s/n 1700-20-207).
- **Instrument LAN** (isolated 192.168.0/24): `.10` FastBi supply,
  `.100` AMI 1700, `.101` this PC, `.1` router.

## Known quirks

- Console is cp1252; `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` is set in `~/.bashrc`
  to address unicode issues.

## What this card does not carry

- **Device facts** — wiring/contact maps, gains, gate stacks,
  validators, calibrated settle times → device card.
- **Campaign state** — goals, recipes in play, reference runs → brief.
- **Session caps** — field/T/voltage limits chosen for a session →
  device card + SAFETIES cell.
- **Conclusions** — no prior-campaign operating points, no device
  leans, no "last time X worked". This card is agent-visible during
  blinded sessions, and operational defaults are also information.

1	# vti-02 / VTI — session brief
2	
3	*Session context for the agent-driven measurement session on the VTI. This file is
4	the `hera-tactical` agent's first message — it names the goal and carries the
5	session-specific facts. Protocol, gates, and boundaries live in your agent prompt;
6	the measurement method is yours to derive from the goal, the cards, and the API
7	reference; this brief does not restate protocol.*
8	
9	## Contract — autonomous
10	
11	This session runs **autonomous (E1)**. After the operator gives the grant (below)
12	**you execute measure cells yourself**; you are not waiting for a keystroke per cell.
13	The operator supervises, is reachable on Slack, and can stop any running cell or
14	withdraw the grant at any time. The deployed measure-notebook policy (`append_exec`)
15	is the hard gate on execution; the grant is the protocol gate on top.
16	
17	## Autonomy — this session's parameters
18	
19	- **Mode:** E1 (autonomous).
20	- **Grant (conditional on VERIFY):** after setup (gate A) and SAFETIES (gate B)
21	  are operator-run and green, you author and land the VERIFY cell; the operator
22	  may then say **"go for autonomy"** without running it. Your first E1 acts are
23	  the read-only kernel-binding probe, then executing VERIFY yourself. The cell's
24	  last output line is the verdict — `VERIFY: ALL GREEN` or `VERIFY: FAIL <item>`
25	  — and the grant keys on that printed line, not your reading of the cell. On
26	  ALL GREEN, record grant + verdict in `session_notes.md` and engage. On any
27	  FAIL, or a missing verdict line, the grant is void: drop to E0, notify the
28	  operator, resume only on explicit re-grant. No measure cell executes before
29	  the green verdict. Until the grant you are in E0 (you propose, the operator
30	  runs).
31	- **Operator + notify:** `Zack — hera-notify --user ZACKG`.
32	- **Auto:** in-envelope measure cells (sweeps, gate sets) that stay inside the
33	  committed validators and pass their precondition reads; field moves within the
34	  device-card field cap; temperature moves via `heater.set_both(T, ratio=0.95)`
35	  within the device-card T cap, honoring the rig card's thermometry and settling
36	  facts (read them before the first elevated-T segment).
37	- **Consent-gated:** any deviation from `ratio = 0.95` in `set_both`.
38	- **Consent-gated (Si):** the Si (DC205) ramp — keep the gate-safe pacing;
39	  `dc205.ramp_rate` is consent-gated (never raise without operator consent).
40	- **Session-banned** (never, regardless of grant): any change to a safety surface —
41	  the SAFETIES validators, the gate operating limits, the field cap, or the
42	  T-setpoint cap; and the banned activities below.
43	- **Withdraw / drop:** the operator can withdraw the grant → you revert to E0. You are
44	  free to stop, notify, and drop to E0 on any device- or rig-safety concern. After any
45	  stop/E0 drop, resume autonomous execution **only on an explicit E1 re-grant**.
46

# vti-02 / VTI — session brief

*Session context for the agent-driven measurement session on the VTI. This file is
the `hera-tactical` agent's first message — it names the goal and carries the
session-specific facts. Protocol, gates, and boundaries live in your agent prompt;
the measurement method is yours to derive from the goal, the cards, and the API
reference; this brief does not restate protocol.*

## Contract — autonomous

This session runs **autonomous (E1)**. After the operator gives the grant (below)
**you execute measure cells yourself**; you are not waiting for a keystroke per cell.
The operator supervises, is reachable on Slack, and can stop any running cell or
withdraw the grant at any time. The deployed measure-notebook policy (`append_exec`)
is the hard gate on execution; the grant is the protocol gate on top.

## Autonomy — this session's parameters

- **Mode:** E1 (autonomous).
- **Grant (conditional on VERIFY):** after setup (gate A) and SAFETIES (gate B)
  are operator-run and green, you author and land the VERIFY cell; the operator
  may then say **"go for autonomy"** without running it. Your first E1 acts are
  the read-only kernel-binding probe, then executing VERIFY yourself. The cell's
  last output line is the verdict — `VERIFY: ALL GREEN` or `VERIFY: FAIL <item>`
  — and the grant keys on that printed line, not your reading of the cell. On
  ALL GREEN, record grant + verdict in `session_notes.md` and engage. On any
  FAIL, or a missing verdict line, the grant is void: drop to E0, notify the
  operator, resume only on explicit re-grant. No measure cell executes before
  the green verdict. Until the grant you are in E0 (you propose, the operator
  runs).
- **Operator + notify:** `Zack — hera-notify --user ZACKG`.
- **Auto:** in-envelope measure cells (sweeps, gate sets) that stay inside the
  committed validators and pass their precondition reads; field moves within the
  device-card field cap; temperature moves via `heater.set_both(T, ratio=0.95)`
  within the device-card T cap, honoring the rig card's thermometry and settling
  facts (read them before the first elevated-T segment).
- **Consent-gated:** any deviation from `ratio = 0.95` in `set_both`.
- **Consent-gated (Si):** the Si (DC205) ramp — keep the gate-safe pacing;
  `dc205.ramp_rate` is consent-gated (never raise without operator consent).
- **Session-banned** (never, regardless of grant): any change to a safety surface —
  the SAFETIES validators, the gate operating limits, the field cap, or the
  T-setpoint cap; and the banned activities below.
- **Withdraw / drop:** the operator can withdraw the grant → you revert to E0. You are
  free to stop, notify, and drop to E0 on any device- or rig-safety concern. After any
  stop/E0 drop, resume autonomous execution **only on an explicit E1 re-grant**.

## Campaign goal

**Determine the stacking order of vti-02 (tetralayer graphene): ABAB (Bernal) vs
ABCA (rhombohedral) vs ABCB (mixed)** — an independent, evidence-cited,
region-resolved call (or a calibrated "cannot tell"), per the output contract below.

## Method

Derive the measurement plan from the goal,
`device_card.md`, `rig_card.md`, the API reference under
`~/measurement_env/docs/api/` (`measureme.md`, `hera-analysis.md`, `drivers.md`,
`sharpelab-nb-drivers.md`), and the data this session produces. Before the first
measure proposal, write the plan — what you will measure, in what order, what each
step establishes, and what would change your mind — to `hera_scratch/plan.md`, and
keep it current as the data comes in. Every proposing cell's markdown cites the
plan step it serves.

The **contact configuration is provided and hardwired** (device card) — there is no
mux to reroute with: a dead provided contact is an operator rewiring problem — flag
it, don't detour. The CNP location and the (n, D) calibration are **not** provided;
establish them in-session before trusting any density or displacement-field scale
derived from the device card's geometry prior.

## Output contract

The call lands as the final cell of the ana notebook, in this form:

1. **Per-region verdict** — one line per measured contact pair: `ABAB` / `ABCA` /
   `ABCB` / `cannot tell`, with a strength word (`weak` / `moderate` / `strong`).
2. **Evidence** — the observations the verdict rests on, each citing run ids
   (`data/<id>`), with the numbers.
3. **Confidence and hedges** — what would overturn the call, what was not measured,
   and why.

## Banned this session

- Probing or extending the gate operating limits: the committed limits are the
  operating box, not a thing to find.
- A standalone Si-gate survey.

## Data isolation — strict

**No prior measurement data exists for you.** Do not read other campaign or session
directories. Your only inputs: this brief, the device card, the rig card, the API
reference, and the data this session produces in `./data/`. Provided up front
(device card): the gate operating limits and the hardwired contact configuration.
**Not** provided — established in-session: the CNP location and the (n, D)
calibration.

## Session arc

1. **Bring-up.** The operator runs the setup section (instrument connect — gate A) and
   the SAFETIES cell (gate B). You author and land the VERIFY cell (below).
2. **Grant.** Operator's **"go for autonomy"** → conditional E1: kernel probe +
   VERIFY execute first; E1 engages on the green verdict.
3. **Autonomous.** Gate C (a cheap liveness check on the provided contact
   configuration, inside the committed limits), then your plan, to the call in the
   ana notebook.
4. **Close-out.** Ask: `return-to-initial` — author and run a close-out cell that
   ramps the field to 0, all three gates (TG, BG, Si) to 0 V at their committed
   pacing, turns both heater ranges off, then prints a readback of field, gates,
   and temperatures; record the readback in `session_notes.md`.

## [VERIFY] at session start

- [x] Magnet at 0 T (read): `print(magnet.field(), magnet._status()['field'])`.
- [x] SAFETIES committed = the device card's gate operating limits; field cap on
      the `magnet.field` validator and the T-setpoint typo-guard cap per the
      device card.
- [x] Base (sample) T holding ≈ 1.2–1.3 K.
- [x] Heaters off (both ranges 0); `T_vaporizer` tracking base.
- [x] Contacts hardwired (no mux this cooldown) per the device card.
- [x] DC205 (Si gate) on its ±100 V range (RNGE 2), output on, reading 0 V.
- [x] Kernel-binding: the first E1 execute is a read-only namespace probe that confirms
      it is bound to the operator's instrument-carrying kernel.

The checks above are the VERIFY cell's content — you author it, read-only by
construction, ending with the machine-readable verdict line (`VERIFY: ALL
GREEN` / `VERIFY: FAIL <item>`). The operator's **"go for autonomy"** may
arrive as soon as the cell is landed; execution of VERIFY is your first E1 act
after the kernel probe, and the grant engages on the printed green verdict
(Autonomy — Grant, above).

## Session notes

Maintain `session_notes.md` per your agent prompt (METHOD / TOOLING / PROTOCOL /
FEEDBACK).

## Session state — in progress

This session is under way; you are picking it up from the instance that ran it so
far. Same kernel, same operator, nothing restarted. The operator returned the rig to its
bring-up state (state0 replayed, gates 0 V, field 0 T) during the handoff and re-ran the
kernel-binding probe in that kernel: the measure notebook's last two executed cells are
that readback and the probe's `KERNEL PROBE: BOUND`. Bring-up, the [VERIFY] list above and
the operator's grant are recorded in `session_notes.md` — **E1 is engaged** and the
kernel-binding check is satisfied; your first E1 execute is the arc's next step. Where
the session stands is in `session_notes.md`, the two notebooks, `./hera_scratch/` and
`./data/`. Read them, then carry on.

The operator's request for the next move is a Landau fan for the stacking call, design and land it.

%matplotlib inline


def _resolve_data_dir():
    """Locate this run's ./data dir from the notebook's own location.

    The ana kernel's cwd is not guaranteed to be the measurement dir, so a
    bare './data' breaks loaders with FileNotFoundError. IPython sets
    globals()['_dh'] to a list whose first entry is the notebook's startup
    cwd (the dir holding the notebook); this survives jupyter-collaboration/
    RTC and any later %cd, so we prefer it. We fall back to Path.cwd() and
    search a few levels up so loading still works if the kernel started inside
    ./data/<id>/. The walk stops before the filesystem root so an unrelated
    top-level 'data' dir can never be matched.
    """
    candidates = []
    dh = globals().get("_dh")
    if dh:
        candidates.append(Path(dh[0]))
    candidates.append(Path.cwd())
    for base in candidates:
        base = Path(base).resolve()
        for d in [base, *base.parents]:
            if d == d.parent:  # filesystem root
                break
            cand = d / "data"
            if cand.is_dir():
                return str(cand)
    return str((Path(candidates[0]) / "data").resolve())


file_path = _resolve_data_dir()


# Open a run by id: run(119) -> Run. Run.col(name) for a column;
# summarize_run(run(119)) for a recipe / range / completeness / T glance.
def run(i):
    return open_run(Path(file_path) / str(i))

"""cnp-and-dline-calibration on gatemap run 5: per-row ridge extraction (two ridges), ratio fit on the
operating window near D = 0, offsets, closure check, realized D = 0 n-window; writes cal params to JSON."""
import json
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD, calc_gate_voltages

rid = 5
g = fan_grids(str(Path(file_path) / str(rid))); rg = resistance_grids(g)
R = np.abs(rg.R["sr1"]); Vbg = g.slow
fs = g.meta["fast_setpoints"]; Vtg = np.asarray(fs[0] if isinstance(fs[0], list) else fs)
c_tg0 = stack_capacitance([(9.5, 3)]); c_bg0 = stack_capacitance([(11, 3)])

pts = []   # (Vbg, Vtg, R, ridge)
for i in range(g.nrows):
    r = gaussian_filter1d(R[i], 1.0)
    pk, _ = find_peaks(r, prominence=0.05 * (r.max() - r.min()) + 5)
    pk = [p for p in pk if 1 < p < g.nfast - 2]
    for p in sorted(pk, key=lambda p: -r[p])[:2]:
        pts.append((Vbg[i], Vtg[p], r[p]))
pts = np.array(pts)
# assign to ridges by distance to the high-D fit of ridge A (rows Vbg < -0.6), then refit each
selA = pts[:, 0] < -0.6
cfA0 = np.polyfit(pts[selA, 0], pts[selA, 1], 1)

ridgeA = pts[np.abs(dist) < 0.08]; ridgeB = pts[(dist < -0.08) & (dist > -0.45)]

def fit(p, lo, hi, label):
    m = (p[:, 0] >= lo) & (p[:, 0] <= hi)
    x, y = p[m, 0], p[m, 1]
    if len(x) < 4: print(f"{label}: {len(x)} rows, skip"); return None
    keep = np.ones(len(x), bool)
    for _ in range(3):
        cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1); res = y - np.polyval(cf, x)
        keep = np.abs(res) < 2.5 * max(np.std(res[keep]), 0.01)
    cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1); res = (y - np.polyval(cf, x))[keep]
    print(f"{label}: {keep.sum()}/{len(x)} rows, Vbg [{lo:+.2f},{hi:+.2f}]: Vtg = {cf[0]:+.4f} Vbg {cf[1]:+.4f}; "
          f"c_bg/c_tg = {-cf[0]:.3f}; rms {np.std(res)*1e3:.1f} mV")
    return cf

import numpy as np

from pathlib import Path

    open_run,

%matplotlib inline


def _resolve_data_dir():
    """Locate this run's ./data dir from the notebook's own location.

    The ana kernel's cwd is not guaranteed to be the measurement dir, so a
    bare './data' breaks loaders with FileNotFoundError. IPython sets
    globals()['_dh'] to a list whose first entry is the notebook's startup
    cwd (the dir holding the notebook); this survives jupyter-collaboration/
    RTC and any later %cd, so we prefer it. We fall back to Path.cwd() and
    search a few levels up so loading still works if the kernel started inside
    ./data/<id>/. The walk stops before the filesystem root so an unrelated
    top-level 'data' dir can never be matched.
    """
    candidates = []
    dh = globals().get("_dh")
    if dh:
        candidates.append(Path(dh[0]))
    candidates.append(Path.cwd())
    for base in candidates:
        base = Path(base).resolve()
        for d in [base, *base.parents]:
            if d == d.parent:  # filesystem root
                break
            cand = d / "data"
            if cand.is_dir():
                return str(cand)
    return str((Path(candidates[0]) / "data").resolve())


file_path = _resolve_data_dir()


# Open a run by id: run(119) -> Run. Run.col(name) for a column;
# summarize_run(run(119)) for a recipe / range / completeness / T glance.
def run(i):
    return open_run(Path(file_path) / str(i))

N, D = calc_nD(Vtg[None, :], Vbg[:, None], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)
m2 = ax[1].pcolormesh(N, D, np.log10(R), shading="nearest", cmap="magma"); fig.colorbar(m2, ax=ax[1], label="log10 |Rxx|")
ax[1].axhline(0, color="y", ls=":", lw=1); ax[1].set_xlabel("n (1e12 cm^-2)"); ax[1].set_ylabel("D (V/nm)"); ax[1].set_title("(n, D) projection, region-A calibration")
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()

# D_offset from the CNP-resistance symmetry in ±D (ridge A only, n within 0.1e12 of the fit line)
rows = []
for i in range(g.nrows):
    vc = cf[0] * Vbg[i] + cf[1]
    if vc < Vtg.min() + 0.03 or vc > Vtg.max() - 0.03: continue
    msk = np.abs(Vtg - vc) < 0.12
    r = gaussian_filter1d(R[i], 1.0); j = np.argmax(np.where(msk, r, -1))
    n_j, D_j = calc_nD(Vtg[j], Vbg[i], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)
    if abs(n_j) < 0.1: rows.append((D_j, r[j]))
rows = np.array(sorted(rows)); k = np.argmin(rows[:, 1]); sel = np.abs(rows[:, 0] - rows[k, 0]) < 0.12
cq = np.polyfit(rows[sel, 0], rows[sel, 1], 2); D0_raw = -cq[1] / (2 * cq[0])
print(f"R_CNP(D) minimum: {rows[k,1]:.0f} Ohm at raw D = {rows[k,0]:+.3f}; parabola vertex raw D = {D0_raw:+.4f} V/nm -> D_offset = {-D0_raw:+.4f}")
plt.figure(figsize=(5, 3.5)); plt.plot(rows[:, 0], rows[:, 1], "o-", ms=3); plt.axvline(D0_raw, color="r", ls="--")
plt.xlabel("raw D (V/nm)"); plt.ylabel("R_CNP ridge A (Ohm)"); plt.title("CNP resistance vs D — vertex = physical D = 0"); plt.show()

## HERA — Step 3: SdH spot check, electron side (`sdh-spot-check`), n = +3.2×10¹² at D = 0, B 0 → 10 T

Calibration from run 5 (ana): c_bg/c_tg = 0.773 (data), c_tg = 2.796 mF/m² (9.5 nm prior), n_offset −0.089×10¹², D_offset −0.013 V/nm (R_CNP(D) symmetry). The D = 0 line inside the validators spans n = −1.27 … +3.27×10¹², so the electron side is the high-|n| side: spot at **n = +3.2×10¹²** → (V_tg, V_bg) = (+0.984, +1.166) V, 16 mV under the TG limit. **Feasibility (Step 2, model table):** F_L = 33.1 T; ABAB pair ≈ 7.5 / 25.6 T (m* 0.028 / 0.061 mₑ), ABCA singleton 33.1 T (m* 0.074); the heavy-ABAB-vs-ABCA split is 7.5 T. Grid: uniform in B (blocking magnet) — 50 mT from 0 to 1 T (MR background only; LK at T_e ≈ 8 K kills m* = 0.06 below ~1.5 T), **10 mT from 1 to 10 T**; 921 points. Dwell: `delay = 0` — each `magnet.field` set blocks through the ramp plus the driver's 3 s settle = 10 τ at τ = 0.3 s / 24 dB, i.e. the lock-in is at the settling floor at every point. Sensitivity fixed at 50 µV (5 kΩ FS): R(B = 0) ≈ 70 Ω is 1.4 % of range, but there is no SdH below ~1.5 T and the MR + SdH maxima at high B need the headroom; the FFT window starts above onset. **Price:** 10 T bare traverse 73 min + 921 × ~3.8 s per-point overhead (settle 3 s + reads) ≈ 58 min → **≈ 2 h 15 m**, ending at **10 T with the gates at the spot** — the hole-side spot check (n = −1.2×10¹²) then rides the magnet down 10 → 0.3 T, never re-traversing. Checkpoints: first 20 points (signal, sensitivity, leakage, field readback tracking setpoints); at ~3 T and ~6 T a partial FFT on the landed record (onset, tone count) — abort if the channel rails or no oscillation content has appeared by 6 T with R flat (then the fan is pointless at this T_e and the read is resolution-limited).
## HERA — Step 3b: SdH spot check, hole side (`sdh-spot-check`), n = −1.2×10¹² at D = 0, riding the magnet 10 → 0.3 T

Run 6 (electron, n = +3.2×10¹²) ends at 10 T with the gates at the spot. The investigation takes both signs (no side prior); the hole side of the D = 0 line reaches only n = −1.27×10¹² (TG −0.3 V limit), so the spot sits at **n = −1.2×10¹²** → (V_tg, V_bg) = (−0.280, −0.463) V. Feasibility (model): F_L = 12.4 T; ABAB pair ≈ 5.3 / 7.1 T (the near-CNP semimetal regime, tones close and balanced — the recipe's stated low-|n| exception), ABCA 12.4 T with m* ≈ 1 mₑ — LK-dead at this rig's T_e ≈ 8 K. **Coverage trade, stated:** this is a cheap preview, not a decisive read — it costs ~35 min over the bare 10 → 0 T ramp the session needs anyway, and a null here is resolvability-limited, not evidence. Grid: 20 mT uniform in B descending, 486 pts, delay 0 (3 s driver settle = 10 τ). Sensitivity 50 µV (5 kΩ FS; R(B = 0) ≈ 250–300 Ω this close to the CNP, MR headroom). Price: 9.7 T traverse 71 min + 486 × ~3.8 s ≈ 31 min → **≈ 1 h 45 m**, ending at 0.3 T. Checkpoints: first 20 points (rail? the CNP side at 10 T could be large), then the ana read at the end together with run 6.

# === SdH spot check, electron side (`sdh-spot-check`): n = +3.2e12 at D = 0 (region-A calibration), B 0 -> 10 T ===
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD

# --- session calibration from run 5 (cnp-and-dline-calibration; ratio data-calibrated, scale = geometry prior) ---
CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
n_spot, D_spot = 3.2, 0.0                       # 1e12 cm^-2, V/nm
Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot = calc_gate_voltages(n_spot, D_spot, CAL["c_tg"], CAL["c_bg"], CAL["n_offset"], CAL["D_offset"])
assert TG_MIN <= Vtg_spot <= TG_MAX and BG_MIN <= Vbg_spot <= BG_MAX, (Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot)
print(f"spot: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm -> (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}) V; "
      f"roundtrip n,D = {calc_nD(Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot, CAL['c_tg'], CAL['c_bg'], CAL['n_offset'], CAL['D_offset'])}")

# --- preconditions (assumed, not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0, _B0 = T_sample(), magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (|B|<0.05: sweep starts at 0), V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (0), "
      f"PS heater {magnet.persistent_switch_on()}, output {magnet.output_enabled()}")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5 and abs(_B0) < 0.05 and abs(k_si()) < 0.01
assert magnet.persistent_switch_on() and magnet.output_enabled()

# --- field grid: uniform in B (blocking rate-limited magnet). 50 mT to 1 T (background only), 10 mT 1 -> 10 T:
B_vec = np.unique(np.round(np.hstack((np.arange(0.0, 1.0, 0.05), np.arange(1.0, 10.0001, 0.01))), 4))
assert B_vec.max() <= B_SESSION_CAP
I_TRIP = 1e-9
# Fixed sensitivity: 50 uV = 5 kOhm full scale at 10 nA (R(B=0) ~ 70 Ohm = 1.4 % FS; MR + SdH maxima at high B size the headroom).
sr1.sensitivity(50e-6)
print(f"B grid: {len(B_vec)} pts, {B_vec[0]} -> {B_vec[-1]} T; sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V, tau {sr1.time_constant()} s (settle_s {magnet.settle_s} s = dwell)")

mc = dict(meas_config); mc["Si (V)"] = k_si(); mc["sample_temperature:"] = _T0
mc["comments"] = f"sdh-spot-check electron: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm (run-5 cal), (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}), B 0 -> 10 T, 10 mT above 1 T, sr1 50 uV"
s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
s.add_comment('sdh-spot-check')
s.add_comment(f'electron side: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12 cm^-2, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm; (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}); '
              f'B 0 -> 10 T uniform-B (50 mT to 1 T, 10 mT above); cal run 5: ratio {CAL["c_bg"]/CAL["c_tg"]:.3f}, n_offset {CAL["n_offset"]:+.3f}e12, D_offset {CAL["D_offset"]:+.3f}')
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, Vbg_spot); s.ramp(k_tg.volt, Vtg_spot)
interruptible_sleep(10)

# row layout: [time, B, T_sample, k_tg.curr, k_bg.curr, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
s.plot(magnet.field, sr1.X); s.plot(magnet.field, sr0.X); s.plot('time', k_tg.curr); s.plot('time', k_bg.curr)

def leak_guard(station, data):
    i_tg, i_bg = abs(float(data[3])), abs(float(data[4]))
    if i_tg > I_TRIP or i_bg > I_TRIP:
        print(f"LEAK TRIP at B={float(data[1]):+.3f} T: |I_tg|={i_tg:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg:.3e} A")
        station.interrupt_requested = True
s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

s.sweep(magnet.field, B_vec, delay=0)
# gates stay at the spot; field stays at 10 T (the hole-side spot check rides it down) — no park here.
print(f"done: B = {magnet.field():+.3f} T, (Vtg, Vbg) = ({k_tg.volt():+.4f}, {k_bg.volt():+.4f})")
=====
## HERA — gatemap re-run at 100 µV (run 4 aborted at the first-rows checkpoint)

Run 4 railed `sr1` (2.18 kΩ, fs 1.09) along the CNP ridge on its first two rows (V_bg = −1.3, D ≈ +0.3 V/nm): the gapped CNP at large |D| already exceeds the 2 kΩ full scale chosen from the D ≈ 0 peaks, so the ridge rows the slope fit needs most would be flat-topped. Aborted at 3 min (interrupted, gates parked at 0). Same map at **100 µV = 10 kΩ full scale** — the expert rule: lose low-R resolution (60 Ω = 0.6 % of range, readable per runs 0–3 at 0.4 %) rather than saturate. Everything else unchanged: TG fast [−0.3, +1.0] V 66 pts, BG slow [−1.3, +1.2] V 63 rows, fast_delay 1 s, leak guard on. Run-4 rate: 48–50 rows/min → 4158 pts ≈ 85 min + turnarounds. Same checkpoints: first rows (rail?), then every ~15 rows.

4	`Station` collects QCoDeS parameters to follow, runs 0D–2D sweeps, and writes
5	each run to a directory (`data.tsv.gz` + `metadata.json`) via a `Writer`.
6	
7	Source: `sweep/sweep.py`, `sweep/db.py`. `import sweep` re-exports the
8	`sweep.sweep` surface (`from .sweep import *`); `sweep.db`, `sweep.raster`,
9	`sweep.sweep_load` are submodules.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Station
14	
15	### `Station(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
16	A collection of followed parameters with sweep methods. `measurement_config`
17	is an arbitrary dict stamped into every run's `metadata.json` (channel→contact,
18	gains, bias, …). `basedir` is the run-directory root; falls back to the module
19	`BASEDIR` (see `set_basedir`) then `os.getcwd()`. The station writes `log.log`
20	into `basedir`, so the directory must exist before construction.
21	
22	### `AsyncStation(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
23	Subclass of `Station`, same constructor and identical I/O / data layout. Reads
24	are parallelized per-instrument (one thread per distinct instrument, one
25	executor reused across a sweep), and same-instrument parameters are
26	batch-read when supported — SR830 `snap` (`SnapReadable`, ≤6 params) or
27	SR86x `get_values` (`BatchReadable`, ≤3 params), else sequential. Use this by
28	default; it produces byte-identical output to `Station`.
29	
30	### `follow_param(param, gain=1.0)` → `Station` · alias **`fp`**
31	Append a QCoDeS parameter to the followed list. The stored column value is
32	**`param() / gain`** (gain division happens at read time). Returns the station,
33	so calls chain: `s.fp(sr0.X, gain).fp(sr0.P)`. For a true-current channel
34	follow it with `gain=1`. Column name is `param.full_name`.
35	
36	### `add_comment(comment)`
37	Append a comment to `metadata['comments']`. **Comments are station-lifetime**:
38	every comment added since construction lands in every subsequent run's
39	metadata — rebuild (or otherwise reset) the station between runs of different
40	intent. `metadata['comments'][0]` is conventionally the recipe slug.
41	
42	### `ramp(param, setpoint)`
43	Logged direct set — calls `param(setpoint)`. It does **not** sub-step; smooth
44	ramping is the driver's own `step`/`inter_delay` (or a driver `ramp_*` method).
45	
46	### `register_run_before(fn, args)` / `register_run_after(fn, args)`
47	Register a hook called at each measured point. `args` must be a tuple. The hook
48	is called `fn(*args, **context)` where **context is injected by parameter
49	name** (via `inspect.signature` — the hook receives only the context keys it
50	declares):
51	
52	| context key | available in | value |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| `station` | before & after | the `Station` |
55	| `writer` | before & after | the active `sweep.db.Writer` |
56	| `data` | after only | the most recent data row (list) |
57	
58	A hook whose parameter is named `station` gets it from context — passing it in
59	`args` too double-binds (`TypeError: multiple values for 'station'`). Order any
60	`args`-supplied params before the context ones. Keyword-only hook params can't
61	be set positionally via `args`; bind them with `functools.partial` (signature
62	is seen through the partial, so injection still works).
63	
64	### Other methods
65	- `measure()` → `SweepResult` — single 0D point.
66	- `watch(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` → `SweepResult` — repeat-measure over
67	  time until `max_duration` (or interrupt).
68	- `read(param, gain=1.0)` / `read_all()` — log a one-off read, no run written.
69	- `plot(x, y, z=None)` / `reset_plots()` — live monitor only, not the data.
70	- `reset()` — clear the interrupted flag so the station can sweep again.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## Sweeps
75	
76	Each sweep method returns a `SweepResult` and writes one run directory. The
77	**data-row column layout** is fixed per method (and matches `metadata['columns']`).
78	`*followed` is the followed-parameter values in `fp` order, each already
79	gain-divided.
80	
81	| method | signature | row layout |
82	|---|---|---|
83	| `measure` | `()` | `[time, *followed]` |
84	| `watch` | `(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` | `[time, *followed]` |
85	| `sweep` | `(param, setpoints, delay=0.0)` | `[time, setpoint, *followed]` |
86	| `multisweep` | `(params, setpointslist, delay=0.0)` | `[time, *setpoints, *followed]` |
87	| `megasweep` | `(slow_param, slow_v, fast_param, fast_v, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, slow, fast, *followed]` |
88	| `multimegasweep` | `(slow_params, slow_v_list, fast_params, fast_v_list, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, *slow, *fast, *followed]` |
89	
90	- **`sweep`** — 1D. Sets `param` to each setpoint, waits `delay`, measures.
91	- **`multisweep`** — 1D, several parameters **co-swept**. `params` and
92	  `setpointslist` are parallel lists; `setpointslist[i]` is the vector for
93	  `params[i]`, and **all vectors must be equal length** (raises otherwise). At
94	  point j every `params[i]` is set to `setpointslist[i][j]` — one path through
95	  N-space, not a grid (e.g. a fixed-D (Vtg, Vbg) line).
96	- **`megasweep`** — 2D grid: outer `slow_param` over `slow_v`, inner
97	  `fast_param` over `fast_v`. `slow_delay` waits once per slow row (at the first
98	  fast point), `fast_delay` waits at every point.
99	- **`multimegasweep`** — 2D grid where each axis is a **co-swept bundle**.
100	  `slow_params`/`slow_v_list` and `fast_params`/`fast_v_list` are parallel
101	  lists; per-axis all vectors must be equal length. The grid is
102	  `len(slow_v) × len(fast_v)`; at each grid point every slow param and every
103	  fast param is set together. Example — field-slow, (Vtg, Vbg)-line-fast:
104	  `s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)`.
105	- **`init_delay`** (2D only) — `True` applies `slow_delay` before the very
106	  first point; `False` skips it (the axis is already parked there).
107	
108	All sweeps are SIGINT-interruptible: an interrupt finishes the current point,
109	sets `metadata['interrupted'] = True`, and marks the station interrupted (call
110	`reset()` or rebuild before the next sweep).
111	
112	### `SweepResult` (dataclass)
113	`SweepResult(basedir, id, metadata, datapath)` — the run root, the integer run
114	id, the final `metadata` dict, and the on-disk `data.tsv.gz` path.
115	
116	---
117	
118	## Module-level helpers (`sweep.*`)
119	
120	- `set_basedir(path)` — set the global `BASEDIR` used when a `Station` is built
121	  without an explicit `basedir`.
122	- `list_measurements(basedir=None)` — render a markdown table of runs in a
123	  basedir.
124	- `measurement_info(i, basedir=None)` — print one run's metadata.
125	- `set_shutdown_handler(fn)` / `request_shutdown()` — register a
126	  ramp-to-safe callback and trigger graceful shutdown (thread-safe; if a sweep
127	  is active it stops after the current point, then calls `fn`). Used by the UPS
128	  monitor.
129	
130	---
131	
132	## Data on disk (`sweep.db`)
133	
134	Each run is a directory `<basedir>/<id>/` with `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless TSV,
135	one row per point), `metadata.json`, and optional blobs (e.g. `plot.png`).
136	
137	### `Writer(basedir, max_id=1_000_000, fsync_every=10)`
138	Creates the run directory at the lowest free integer id under `basedir`
139	(`.id`, `.dir`). `add_point(point)` / `add_points(points)` append rows
140	(fsynced every `fsync_every` points); `add_blob(name, bytes)` writes a sidecar
141	file (name may not be `data.tsv`/`data.tsv.gz`/`metadata.json`). `.metadata` is
142	a free dict saved to `metadata.json` on `close()`; on close the uncompressed
143	`data.tsv` is gzipped to `data.tsv.gz` (verified, then the plaintext removed).
144	Use as a context manager.
145	
146	### `Reader(basedir, id)`
147	Reads a run back. `.metadata` (migrated to the current schema via
148	`migrate_metadata`), iteration yields rows of **strings** (no type conversion),
149	`all_data()` returns all rows, `blob(name)` reads a sidecar. `.datapath` is the
150	`data.tsv.gz` path. Use as a context manager. For numeric loads,
151	`np.loadtxt(reader.datapath, …)` or `hera.analysis.open_run`.
152	
153	### Metadata keys written per sweep type
154	Common to all: `version`, `type` (`0D`/`1D`/`2D`), `function`, `columns`,
155	`comments`, `measurement_config`, `instruments`, `interrupted`, `start_time`,
156	`end_time`.
157	
158	| function | additional keys |
159	|---|---|
160	| `sweep` | `param`, `setpoints`, `delay` |
161	| `multisweep` | `params`, `setpoints` (list of per-param vectors), `delay` |
162	| `megasweep` | `slow_param`, `fast_param`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
163	| `multimegasweep` | `slow_params`, `fast_params`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
164	| `watch` | `delay`, `max_duration` |
165	
166	Two schemas coexist in older data — singular (`param`, `slow_param`) vs current
167	plural (`params`, `slow_params`). Read through `sweep.sweep_load` or
168	`hera.analysis.open_run`; don't hand-roll key access.
169	
170	---
171	
172	## Polygon rasters (`sweep.raster`)
173	
174	Helpers for sweeping/plotting an arbitrary polygon region of a 2-D plane (e.g. a
175	bounded (Vtg, Vbg) window). A `multimegasweep` runs the rasterized point order;
176	these turn polygon vertices into that point list and back into a plot mesh.
177	
178	### `rasterize(vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs, ys)`
179	The x/y coordinates of the grid points **inside** the polygon. `vertices` is
180	`(N, 2)`; `nx`/`ny` are grid points per axis over the bounding box; `fast_axis`
181	is 0 if x is the inner (fast) axis, 1 if y; `rev_x`/`rev_y` reverse a sweep
182	direction. Returns two 1-D arrays in raster order — feed them as the co-swept
183	fast/slow vectors of a `multimegasweep`.
184	
185	### `pcolorize_data(zs, vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`
186	Bin measured values `zs` (in rasterized point order) back onto the regular
187	bounding mesh for `plt.pcolormesh(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`. Cells outside the
188	polygon are `NaN`. The `nx`/`ny`/`fast_axis`/`rev_*` arguments must match the
189	`rasterize` call that produced the sweep.
190	
191	### `random_ngon_vertices(n)` → `(n, 2)` vertices
192	A random simple-ish n-gon, for tests/demos.

| `multimegasweep` | `slow_params`, `fast_params`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `watch` | `delay`, `max_duration` |

Two schemas coexist in older data — singular (`param`, `slow_param`) vs current
plural (`params`, `slow_params`). Read through `sweep.sweep_load` or
`hera.analysis.open_run`; don't hand-roll key access.

---

## Polygon rasters (`sweep.raster`)

Helpers for sweeping/plotting an arbitrary polygon region of a 2-D plane (e.g. a
bounded (Vtg, Vbg) window). A `multimegasweep` runs the rasterized point order;
these turn polygon vertices into that point list and back into a plot mesh.

### `rasterize(vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs, ys)`
The x/y coordinates of the grid points **inside** the polygon. `vertices` is
`(N, 2)`; `nx`/`ny` are grid points per axis over the bounding box; `fast_axis`
is 0 if x is the inner (fast) axis, 1 if y; `rev_x`/`rev_y` reverse a sweep
direction. Returns two 1-D arrays in raster order — feed them as the co-swept
fast/slow vectors of a `multimegasweep`.

### `pcolorize_data(zs, vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`
Bin measured values `zs` (in rasterized point order) back onto the regular
bounding mesh for `plt.pcolormesh(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`. Cells outside the
polygon are `NaN`. The `nx`/`ny`/`fast_axis`/`rev_*` arguments must match the
`rasterize` call that produced the sweep.

### `random_ngon_vertices(n)` → `(n, 2)` vertices
A random simple-ish n-gon, for tests/demos.

- `density(V_tg, V_bg)` → n `(m⁻²)`.
- `displacement_field(V_tg, V_bg)` → D `(V/m)`.
- `n_D(V_tg, V_bg)` → `(n, D)`.
- `from_thicknesses(t_tg, t_bg, t_bgSiO2=0.0, *, n_offset=0.0, D_offset=0.0, kappa_hBN=3.0, kappa_SiO2=3.9)` — build from gate-stack geometry (metres) instead of areal capacitances; `t_bgSiO2=0` for a metal/graphite back gate.

All accept scalars or arrays. Physical constants come from `scipy.constants`.

### `luttinger_frequency(n)` → `np.ndarray`
Full-density Onsager (SdH) frequency `F = |n|·h / (4·e)`, in Tesla, for a
single Fermi surface carrying the full density. **`n` is in SI m⁻²** — feed
`GateCalibration.density` output directly. The 4 is the spin×valley Landau
degeneracy; returns the `|n|` form (positive for either carrier sign).

# === Gate C — liveness + gross gate safety: gate-current-sanity-check (first-session branch) ===
# Four legs, each gate 0 -> each card limit with the other parked at 0, 101 pts, delay 1 s,
# nplci=10 on the gate-current channels (pA floor). Lock-in X on sr1 (B_1-B_2) + sr0 (drain)
# answer "is the device alive on the provided contacts"; gate currents answer "is it safe".
# Automatic abort: |I_gate| > 1 nA on either Keithley trips the sweep (no operator eyes in E1).
from sharpelab_nb.autorange import autorange_sr830s

# --- preconditions (state this cell assumes but does not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0 = T_sample(); _B0 = magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (expect 1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (expect |B|<0.02), "
      f"V_tg = {k_tg.volt():+.3f}, V_bg = {k_bg.volt():+.3f}, V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (expect 0)")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5, f"T_sample {_T0} K off base"
assert abs(_B0) < 0.02, f"magnet not at zero: {_B0} T"
assert abs(k_si()) < 0.01, "Si gate not at 0"

legs = [(k_tg, TG_MAX), (k_tg, TG_MIN), (k_bg, BG_MAX), (k_bg, BG_MIN)]
n_pts, delay = 101, 1.0
I_TRIP = 1e-9   # A — hard abort threshold on either gate current

# pA-floor readback on the gate-current channels (reset at the end if no leg tripped)
k_tg.nplci(10); k_bg.nplci(10)

# sr1 sensitivity sized for an unknown Rxx: 500 uV = 50 kOhm full scale at I_bias = 10 nA
# (drive 1 V / 100 MOhm, as the operator set it); autorange hook tracks from there.
sr1.sensitivity(500e-6)
print(f"drive {sr1.amplitude()} V @ {sr1.frequency()} Hz -> I_bias ~ {sr1.amplitude()/100e6*1e9:.1f} nA; "
      f"sr0 sens {sr0.sensitivity()} V, sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V, tau {sr1.time_constant()} s")

tripped = []
for gate, v_end in legs:
    other = k_bg if gate is k_tg else k_tg
    mc = dict(meas_config); mc["comments"] = f"gate-current-sanity-check: {gate.name} 0 -> {v_end:+g} V, other gate 0, Si 0, B 0"
    s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
    s.add_comment('gate-current-sanity-check')
    s.add_comment(f'gate: {gate.name}; leg: 0 -> {v_end:+g} V (card limit); {other.name} parked 0; Vsi = 0; B = 0')
    s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0); s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)
    xp = gate.volt
    # row layout: [time, setpoint, other.volt, gate.curr, other.curr, T_sample, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
    s.fp(other.volt).fp(gate.curr).fp(other.curr).fp(T_sample)
    s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
    s.plot(xp, k_tg.curr); s.plot(xp, k_bg.curr)
    s.plot(xp, sr1.X); s.plot(xp, sr0.X)
    s.register_run_before(autorange_sr830s, (sr0, [sr1]))

    def leak_guard(station, data, _gate=gate):
        i_g, i_o = abs(float(data[3])), abs(float(data[4]))
        if i_g > I_TRIP or i_o > I_TRIP:
            print(f"LEAK TRIP on {_gate.name} leg at V = {float(data[1]):+.3f} V: |I_swept| = {i_g:.3e}, |I_other| = {i_o:.3e} A")
            tripped.append((_gate.name, float(data[1]), i_g, i_o))
            station.interrupt_requested = True
    s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

    try:
        s.sweep(gate.volt, np.linspace(0, v_end, n_pts), delay=delay)
    finally:
        s.ramp(gate.volt, 0)
    if tripped:
        break

if tripped:
    print("STOP — a leg tripped the leakage guard; nplci left at 10, gates parked at 0:", tripped)
else:
    k_tg.nplci(1); k_bg.nplci(1)
    print("all four legs ran without a leakage trip; nplci reset to 1")
    print("k_tg.volt validator:", k_tg.volt.vals, "| k_bg.volt validator:", k_bg.volt.vals)

"""Runs 6 (e-side, n=+3.2e12, 0->10 T) and 7 (h-side, n=-1.2e12, 10->0.3 T): raw R(B), sdh_onset, sdh_fft."""
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pathlib import Path
from hera.analysis import open_run, resolve_channels, sdh_onset, sdh_fft, SdhOnsetError, luttinger_frequency
D = Path("data")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(16, 8))
for k, (rid, lab) in enumerate([(6, "e n=+3.2e12"), (7, "h n=-1.2e12")]):
    r = open_run(D / str(rid)); ch = {c.cid: c for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
    B = r.col("magnet_field"); I = r.col("sr0_X") / ch["sr0"].gain
    R = (r.col("sr1_X") / ch["sr1"].gain) / I
    o = np.argsort(B); B, R, I = B[o], R[o], I[o]
    T = r.col("T_sample")[o]
    print(f"\n=== run {rid} {lab}: {len(B)} pts, B {B.min():.2f}-{B.max():.2f} T, R {R.min():.1f}..{R.max():.1f} Ohm, I {I.mean()*1e9:.2f} nA, T {T.min():.3f}-{T.max():.3f} K, interrupted={r.interrupted}")
    ax[k, 0].plot(B, R, lw=0.7); ax[k, 0].set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax[k, 0].set_ylabel("Rxx (Ohm)"); ax[k, 0].set_title(f"run {rid} {lab} raw")
    fs = 50e-6 / 10e-9
    try:
        so = sdh_onset(R, B, b_lo=1.0, r_full_scale=fs)
        print(so.summary())
    except SdhOnsetError as e:
        print("sdh_onset:", e)
    for blo, bhi in [(1.5, 10.0), (3.0, 10.0)]:
        m = (B >= blo) & (B <= bhi)
        f, sp = sdh_fft(R[m][:, None], B[m], b_range=None, bg_degree=5, log=False, nfft=2048)
        sp = sp[0]; sel = (f > 2) & (f < 120)
        pk = f[sel][np.argsort(sp[sel])[::-1][:6]]

1	# `sharpelab_nb.drivers` API Reference
2	
3	Instrument drivers in `src/sharpelab_nb/drivers/`, re-exported from the package:
4	
5	```python
6	from sharpelab_nb.drivers import SRS_DC205, Yokogawa7651, ANC350
7	```
8	
9	The `drivers` package (`src/drivers/`: `FastBi1K5`, `QSwitch`, `ContactMux`,
10	the VTI `SRS_DC205`, …) is documented separately in
11	[`drivers.md`](drivers.md).
12	
13	---
14	
15	## `SRS_DC205` — DC voltage source (fixed-duration ramp)
16	
17	`SRS_DC205(name, address, *, ramp_num_points=100, ramp_wait_time=0.01, **kwargs)`.
18	Serial `VisaInstrument` (115200 baud).
19	
20	| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
21	|---|---|---|---|
22	| `voltage` | V | R/W | raw setpoint (7 dp) |
23	| `smart_voltage` | V | R/W | set → `ramp_voltage` |
24	| `voltage_range` | — | R/W | 0: ±1 V, 1: ±10 V, 2: ±100 V |
25	| `output` | 0/1 | R/W | output enable |
26	
27	- **`ramp_voltage(volt)`** — software ramp from the current reading over
28	  `ramp_num_points` steps spaced `ramp_wait_time` apart (so the duration is
29	  roughly fixed regardless of ΔV), **plus a mandatory 10 s settle when
30	  `|Δvolt| > 0.1 V`**. (The VTI `drivers.SRS_DC205` of the same name uses
31	  rate-based (`ramp_rate` V/s) semantics and has no fixed settle — they are not
32	  interchangeable.)
33	
34	---
35	
36	## `Yokogawa7651` — programmable DC source (pre-SCPI, write-only cached)
37	
38	`Yokogawa7651(name, address, *, coil_constant=None, **kwargs)`. The 7651 is
39	pre-SCPI (no `*IDN?`) and cannot report programmed values back over the bus, so
40	**all set parameters are write-only with a software cache**.
41	
42	| parameter | unit | R/W | range / notes |
43	|---|---|---|---|
44	| `volt` | V | W | ±30 V |
45	| `current` | A | W | ±0.12 A |
46	| `field` | T | W | requires `coil_constant=`; range = ±0.12·|coil| |
47	| `mode` | — | W | `'VOLT'` (F1;) / `'CURR'` (F5;) |
48	| `output` | bool | W | output enable |
49	
50	- After a kernel restart the cache is empty, so the ramp methods raise unless
51	  the cache is seeded first: **`set_voltage_cache(value)`** /
52	  **`set_current_cache(value)`**, or pass `start=` to the ramp call.
53	- **`ramp_voltage(target, step=0.01, delay=0.05, start=None)`** /
54	  **`ramp_current(target, step=0.001, delay=0.05, start=None)`** — software ramp
55	  from the cached (or `start=`) value; `step` must be `> 0`.
56	- When `coil_constant` is given, `field.step`/`field.inter_delay` are
57	  pre-configured for safe ramping (0.1 mT / 0.1 s ⇒ ~1 mT/s).
58	- `trigger()` sends `E;` (normally automatic after each set). `get_idn()`
59	  returns a static dict.
60	
61	---
62	
63	## `ANC350` — attocube piezo motion controller (rotator)
64	
65	`ANC350(name, dll_dir, *, device_no=0, num_axes=3, **kwargs)`. Loads
66	`anc350v2.dll`/`libusb0.dll` from `dll_dir`; exposes `num_axes` axes as a
67	`ChannelTuple` at `.axes` (each an `ANC350Axis`).
68	
69	### `ANC350Axis` (one stepper axis)
70	| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
71	|---|---|---|---|
72	| `status` | — | R | raw status int (decode via `is_moving`/`is_at_eot`/`has_sensor_error`/`is_sensor_disconnected`) |
73	| `position` | counts | R | raw sensor int32 (INT32_MAX when sensor power is off — the toploader default) |
74	| `rotation_count` | — | R | full-rotation counter |
75	| `amplitude` | mV | R/W | step drive amplitude, 0–70 000 |
76	| `frequency` | Hz | R/W | step frequency, 1–2000 |
77	| `dc_level` | mV | R/W | constant DC for fine positioning (output must be enabled) |
78	| `output_enabled` | bool | W | HV output; reads a software tri-state cache (True/False/None) — `set_output_cache()` to seed after restart |
79	
80	Methods: `step(direction, count=1, *, wait=True, timeout=60.0, poll_interval=0.05)`
81	(±1 = forward/backward), `step_continuous(direction)`, `stop()`,
82	`wait_until_idle(…)`. `step`/`step_continuous` refuse to run unless the output
83	cache is `True`.
84	
85	---
86	
87	## Lock-in servo (`lockin_servo`)
88	
89	Closed-loop positioning of an `ANC350Axis` against a lock-in voltage readback.
90	Not re-exported from the package — import from
91	`sharpelab_nb.drivers.lockin_servo`.
92	
93	### `bring_up_servo_axis(name, axis, readback, *, amplitude_mv=60_000, frequency_hz=100, direction_sign=None, settle_time=0.5, v_min=-50e-3, v_max=+50e-3, tolerance=25e-6, max_iterations=200, step_count=1)` → `LockinServoedAxis`
94	One-call bring-up: set amplitude/frequency, enable HV output, resolve
95	`direction_sign` (if `None`, **physically steps the rotator** via
96	`calibrate_direction_sign` and prints the result to cache), and construct the
97	servo. `amplitude_mv` is millivolts (60 000 = 60 V).
98	
99	### `LockinServoedAxis(name, *, axis, readback, direction_sign, v_min, v_max, tolerance=25e-6, settle_time=0.5, max_iterations=200, step_count=1)`
100	| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
101	|---|---|---|---|
102	| `voltage` | V | R | one-shot read of the underlying readback |
103	| `target_voltage` | V | R/W | **set runs the servo loop synchronously**; get = last target (or None) |
104	| `last_iterations` | — | R | iterations used by the last run |
105	| `last_residual` | V | R | `abs(target − final)` of the last run |
106	
107	`set` of `target_voltage` raises `ServoTimeout` if `max_iterations` is exceeded.
108	`abort()` requests the in-progress loop to stop (does not call `axis.stop()`).
109	`direction_sign` and `axis` are properties.
110	
111	### `thermalized_setpoint(servo, readback_lockin, *, name=None, full_amp=None, off_amp=0.004, wait_s=60.0)` → `Parameter`
112	Wrap a servo move + sensor-excitation cool-down into one settable-only
113	`Parameter` (use as a sweep's slow axis): restore excitation → servo to target
114	→ drop excitation to `off_amp` → wait `wait_s` for the stage to thermalize.
115	After each set the lock-in amplitude is left at `off_amp`, so the followed
116	readback is noise during the read window — the meaningful axis is the setpoint.
117	
118	### `calibrate_direction_sign(axis, readback, *, settle_time, noise_samples=5, noise_threshold=None, max_test_steps=10)` → `(sign, n_steps)`
119	Resolve step polarity empirically: issue forward steps until `readback` moves
120	past the noise threshold, return `+1` if it rose else `-1` (with the step count
121	used). `settle_time` is required. Called automatically by `bring_up_servo_axis`
122	when `direction_sign=None`.
123

Not re-exported from the package — import from
`sharpelab_nb.drivers.lockin_servo`.

### `bring_up_servo_axis(name, axis, readback, *, amplitude_mv=60_000, frequency_hz=100, direction_sign=None, settle_time=0.5, v_min=-50e-3, v_max=+50e-3, tolerance=25e-6, max_iterations=200, step_count=1)` → `LockinServoedAxis`
One-call bring-up: set amplitude/frequency, enable HV output, resolve
`direction_sign` (if `None`, **physically steps the rotator** via
`calibrate_direction_sign` and prints the result to cache), and construct the
servo. `amplitude_mv` is millivolts (60 000 = 60 V).

### `LockinServoedAxis(name, *, axis, readback, direction_sign, v_min, v_max, tolerance=25e-6, settle_time=0.5, max_iterations=200, step_count=1)`
| parameter | unit | R/W | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voltage` | V | R | one-shot read of the underlying readback |
| `target_voltage` | V | R/W | **set runs the servo loop synchronously**; get = last target (or None) |
| `last_iterations` | — | R | iterations used by the last run |
| `last_residual` | V | R | `abs(target − final)` of the last run |

`set` of `target_voltage` raises `ServoTimeout` if `max_iterations` is exceeded.
`abort()` requests the in-progress loop to stop (does not call `axis.stop()`).
`direction_sign` and `axis` are properties.

### `thermalized_setpoint(servo, readback_lockin, *, name=None, full_amp=None, off_amp=0.004, wait_s=60.0)` → `Parameter`
Wrap a servo move + sensor-excitation cool-down into one settable-only
`Parameter` (use as a sweep's slow axis): restore excitation → servo to target
→ drop excitation to `off_amp` → wait `wait_s` for the stage to thermalize.
After each set the lock-in amplitude is left at `off_amp`, so the followed
readback is noise during the read window — the meaningful axis is the setpoint.

### `calibrate_direction_sign(axis, readback, *, settle_time, noise_samples=5, noise_threshold=None, max_test_steps=10)` → `(sign, n_steps)`
Resolve step polarity empirically: issue forward steps until `readback` moves
past the noise threshold, return `+1` if it rose else `-1` (with the step count
used). `settle_time` is required. Called automatically by `bring_up_servo_axis`
when `direction_sign=None`.
